author: [deleted]
body:
> Was going Dragon Knight a mistake or are the classes even enough that it doesn't really matter? I spec'd towards DK based on suggestions I read at the beginning of the year. Seemed like a solid choice. Yesterday I read quite a few posts suggesting DK was actually terrible. Not a huge deal, just curious if I ended up choosing one of the worst options.

Absolutely not. I was DK in much of tier 8 and it was great. If you go with the Beastmaster build with a good pet (I recommend Arcane Slime, or War Horse for raids) it's probably the strongest T7 class IMO. You can play it as a Beastmaster or just use it as a mage class (I actually was able to use it with a melee build because I had a great weapon for it). It is one of my favorite classes in the game.

As a side note, rarely is any class so underpowered that you can't make it work. You will often find people talking trash about a certain class; do not take single instances of this at face value. You can make any build you want work if you grind hard enough for gear; it is just easier to succeed with some builds than others.

> I've seen people say that weapon drops from mobs are terrible but gear drops can be okay. All my gear is currently from mobs. How else do people obtain gear? I'm guessing if not from mobs, then from kingdom related events? Perhaps I misread this?

Raids can drop super good items of all types but it is rare so consider yourself lucky if you get a good raid boss item.

> Are Yeti Overcoats and Crystalis still great t7 items?

Yeti Overcoat is a great piece of armor. I'm level 198 and I'm still using a 114% superior version (which I masterforged) because it's the only armor I have with good resistance.

Crystalis is a particularly fantastic item if you are a Dragon Knight/Beastmaster because when your pet is your main source of damage output you don't care if your weapon has high stats. It also still works the same way for other classes in gauntlets.

> Any suggestions for t7 accessories? I've been rocking Troll Charms forever and feel like there's probably much better items I should be using.

High quality Troll's Charms are solid accessories. However, you definitely should get accessories which will allow you to use Druid's buffs without downsides (and without needing a Crystalis). You will need:

* either and Arch-Gadget or a Ring of Day
* either an Arch-Gizmo or a Ring of Night

All of these are currently available from the Age-Old Mimic, one of this month's raid bosses. Make sure you get them before the month ends because Druid buffs are super duper powerful.

> is there any advantage to claiming new territory that I cannot regularly visit?

You will get achievements for claiming a large number of territories but that is it.

> How does preferred weapon for a class and specialization work? If I am a DK with a sword, for example, does it then hurt my Ranger specialization since I am not using a bow? Does this only matter if I choose the Ranger sprite as my main image?

You have one list of your preferred weapons and it is all of the weapon types which are preferred by either your class OR your specialization. When you are using a preferred weapon type, you get a 5% bonus to att/mag. You can only get the buff once; using a weapon type preferred by both class and spec does not grant you it twice.
